judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely formal substitution of the attestation clause; the only oddity is that it cites 'Form UML-002 (4/91)' when the policy form is UML 002 (1/91).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-cited edition date is a small mismatch with the base form actually attached, but nothing turns on the attestation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cancellation by surrender or by mailing notice 'stating when thereafter the cancellation shall be effective' — definite and conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the opening of Condition 12 (c055) without expressly deleting it, so two insured-cancellation provisions coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in sentence; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces (a)-(e) below and is consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise statutory-style rule with a stated 10-day notice and objective 60-day/renewal triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 (c092) promises sixty days' written notice of any cancellation, and Condition 12 (c055) states thirty days, so the notice period cannot be determined from this paragraph alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Non-payment cancellation on 10 days' notice, keyed to failure to discharge premium obligations when due; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the sixty-day notice promised by Endorsement No. 3 (c092) and with the thirty days in Condition 12 (c055); the Pay Plan Endorsement (c098) supplies the due dates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial change in the risk assumed' and 'substantial breaches of contractual duties, conditions or warranties' are evaluative standards, though they are lifted from the Wisconsin statute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 10-day notice is contradicted by Endorsement No. 3's sixty days (c092) and by Condition 12's thirty days (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening words 'if in addition to the right of the Company to cancel as provided for in paragraph (b) and (c) above and provided that if...' are grammatically broken, obscuring whether the paragraph adds to or qualifies the earlier rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared policy period is a single year, so this paragraph is dormant, but it also omits paragraph (a) from its cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The named insured shall have a right te to renewal' contains a doubled word, and a guaranteed renewal 'on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks' is an open-ended promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its sixty-day non-renewal notice is consistent with Endorsement No. 3 (c092) but sits against the ten-day cancellation rules in (a)-(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence makes full compliance with all terms a condition precedent while the second entitles 'any person or organization' to recover to the extent of the insurance afforded — the two sentences point in opposite directions within one clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes the original Action Against Company condition (c049) and is itself qualified by the Wisconsin Declarations provision (c073), which forbids forfeiture for non-material breaches, undercutting the condition-precedent sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The company will be entitled to a recovery only after the insured has been fully compensated for damages' is a clean made-whole rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is added to the subrogation waterfall (c053), whose stated order of apportionment reimburses interests and the company before any balance goes to the insured — the two orderings are hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory language reproduced with a mis-cited section ('637.09' for 631.09), but the substantive rule about agent knowledge is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts Condition 11 (c054), which states that notice to or knowledge of any agent effects no waiver or change and does not estop the company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reproduces Wis. Stat. s.631.11(2)-(3) with its own express carve-out for premium tender; precise as statutes go.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the warranty in Condition 13 (c056) and the condition-precedent sentence in c070, but as a statutory overlay rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any insured subject of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act' is garbled ('subject of' for 'subject to'), and the closing limitation 'with respect to their duties under pension or employee benefit plans' may or may not qualify the whole exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses fiduciary or benefit-plan liability, so the difficulty is internal to the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b), 'property used by any Insured hereunder', is extraordinarily broad and its outer boundary is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy already contains a narrower care-custody-and-control exclusion in the base form (c024), qualified 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance', and this endorsement does not say it replaces it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Directors and officers are excluded from this contract for liability arising out of wrongful acts' is loosely drafted — it excludes persons rather than coverage, leaving the operation of the exclusion uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out in c078 restores liability for personal injury, bodily injury, property damage, hospital professional liability and advertisers liability, which is essentially everything the policy insures, so the exclusion may have no work to do.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely by reason of their being directors or officers of the company' uses 'the company', a term the policy elsewhere reserves for the insurer, creating a genuine referential ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy's own defined term 'company' means Ohio Hospital Insurance Company, so read literally this definition points at the wrong entity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out lists 'hospital professional liability' and 'adverisers liability', neither of which is a defined term in this policy, and together the listed categories exhaust the coverage grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be reconciled with the insuring agreement (c002), which insures only personal injury, property damage and advertising liability, nor with the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082), which excludes the very hospital professional liability this carve-out preserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence removing 'any injury arising out of discrimination' from personal injury; 'arising out of' is broad but the rule is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts limb (5) of the Personal Injury definition (c035), which expressly includes racial or religious discrimination not committed by or on behalf of the insured, and overlaps with FF-15 (c058).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is heavily truncated in reproduction, but the substance is a standard total asbestos exclusion covering manufacture, mining, use and exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses asbestos; the only interface is the defence disclaimer in c081.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-duty-to-defend statement for asbestos suits; blunt and definite in intent even though the reproduced text is broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the Supplementary Payments obligation to defend suits 'even if groundless, false or fraudulent' (c004), and the two are not expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hospital umbrella that excludes 'the furnishing of professional health care services' is a striking exclusion, and the reach of 'arising out of the rendering of or failure to render' plus limb (b)'s peer-review language is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared easily with the Aggregate Limits Endorsement's 'any professional liability hazard' aggregate (c084), the Cross Suits professional carve-out (c060), the D&O carve-out for hospital professional liability (c078), the Contingent Excess endorsement (c100-c104) and the professional liability limits endorsement (c121).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole professional coverage turns on the phrase 'entities or individuals that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund', a status test that is neither defined nor obviously binary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the Contingent Excess endorsement (c100-c102), which uses a different formula (entities 'defined by Wisconsin Statute 655.001 as a health care provider') and with c104, which disapplies a differently-dated version of this very form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It introduces 'any professional liability hazard' into the aggregate limit without defining that term, unlike 'products hazard' and 'completed operations hazard' which are defined — a general term standing beside enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces c013 while assuming professional liability coverage exists, in tension with the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082); the amounts it points to are then changed again by Endorsement No. 4 (c109).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named insureds coupled with a disclaimer of 'automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them'; the list itself is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Named Insured definition (c020), which automatically embraces subsidiaries and controlled organizations, and against later endorsements adding entities piecemeal (c115, c117, c120), so whether an unlisted affiliate is insured is genuinely open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single mechanical rule deeming notice to the Item 1 insured notice to all; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the first-named-insured provision at the end of Condition 12 (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'unless otherwise stated herein' proviso matches the endorsement's own effective date field.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a vague limitation on additional insured status that generates recurring disputes about scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the omnibus insured limb for persons owed insurance by written contract (c029) and with c031, which confers insured status on anyone insured under the underlying policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise limitation of Form 009-400 to Med-Health Financial Services; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Collection Agency exclusion itself (c099) is drafted to apply to 'the Insured' generally, so the two must be read together to confine it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence promising sixty days' written notice 'in the event of cancellation or non-renewal' with no exception, not even for non-payment of premium.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the ten-day notice periods in the Wisconsin Cancellation endorsement (c065, c066, c067) and the thirty days in Condition 12 (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It identifies the replaced exclusion by description rather than by paragraph letter, and the description does not track the base-form pollution exclusion word for word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether it fully supplants the base pollution exclusion with its 'sudden and accidental' carve-back (c028) turns on that imperfect match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard ISO CG 21 49 total pollution exclusion; long but structured, with an express hostile-fire carve-back and definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces c028 by operation of c093 and is internally consistent with the pollutants definition in c096.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean cleanup-cost and governmental-claim exclusion in familiar terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c094 and with the ultimate net loss definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant' is the single most frequently construed definition in liability insurance because 'irritant or contaminant' has no natural boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only inside the total pollution exclusion and matches the language of c094.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It declares payments 'past due' but attaches no stated consequence, leaving the sentence operatively incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consequence has to be imported from the Wisconsin non-payment cancellation paragraph (c066) and Item 6's short-rate minimum premium provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature' is a general formula whose reach over ordinary collection activity is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: On its face it applies to 'the Insured' at large, whereas Endorsement No. 2 (c090) confines it to Med-Health Financial Services; the two texts describe different scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat denial of medical malpractice coverage for any statutory health care provider, later contradicted within the same endorsement by the contingency grant — the opening sentence overstates its own effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the Professional Services Excluded carve-out (c083), the professional liability aggregate in c084 and the increased professional limits in c121, all of which assume some professional cover exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subsidiaries of holding companies of the named insured' expands a statutory definition by contract in a way that is genuinely unclear in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It intersects with the Named Insured definition's subsidiary and control language (c020) and with the closed list in c085, which do not use the same corporate vocabulary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-condition contingency with the further qualifier 'identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes', a phrase whose referent is not supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 7's schedule of underlying insurance identifies nothing as listed for contingency purposes, so the trigger points to something that does not exist in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves 'appropriate' wholly undefined, though the discretion is expressly reserved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same formula reappears in c122, and neither is tied to the Pay Plan Endorsement's fixed instalments (c097-c098).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies 'Form No. 035(12/87) Professional Services Excluded', but the form actually attached is 035 WI (1/94) — a mis-citation that may leave the intended disapplication inoperative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement schedule and the attached exclusion (c082) both show the 1/94 Wisconsin edition, so the cross-reference does not match anything in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy' and then merely recites a statute without stating an operative change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Hospital Professional Liability coverage part is attached to this umbrella form, whose territory clause (c014) says 'anywhere'; and Endorsement No. 5 (c111) declares this very form deleted and null and void while it remains in the assembled policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Indemnity for 'legal or other expenses necessarily incurred ... in determining which insurer shall bear the loss' is an unusual and loosely bounded promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the ultimate net loss definition (c033), which excludes legal expenses from loss, and against the Other Insurance clause (c052), which itself allocates between insurers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says coverage 'shall not apply to trebled damages' and then that the company will pay one-third of the total sum, and separately excludes plaintiff's legal fees twice by different routes — the mechanics are self-tangling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 (c111) deletes Form 009-133 and declares it null and void, yet the form remains in the assembled policy and on the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: But note the endorsement it introduces is dated 05/06/1996 while stating inception-date effectiveness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the policy limits in Item 2', but Item 2 of the Declarations is the Policy Period and the limits are in Item 3, and the consideration line is left blank ('additional premium of $ ___') — two mechanical defects that go to whether the change is effective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations state $18,000,000 each occurrence and a $9,000,000 aggregate, while this endorsement states $20,000,000/$20,000,000 and the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) restates the limit provision yet again, leaving the operative limit unresolved on the face of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its stated inception-date effectiveness sits oddly with the 06/21/1996 issue date of the endorsement it introduces.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite deletion of two identified forms; the only oddity is deleting a form 'considered null and void' retrospectively to inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both deleted forms (c107 Trebled Damages and c105 Policy Territory 10/92) remain physically in the policy and on the Schedule of Endorsements, so the assembled instrument contains provisions it says are void.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line attachment of Form 009-118 (2/96); plain, though the sentence lacks a full stop.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached replacement (c113) still amends a Hospital Professional Liability coverage part that is not present in this umbrella policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its predecessor it recites a statute without stating any operative amendment, and the recital is introduced as 's.655.27(5)(a)2' but quoted as 's.655.27(5)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to amend territory provisions of a Hospital Professional Liability coverage part that does not form part of this umbrella policy, whose own territory clause (c014) is 'anywhere'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement's stated effective date is 07/08/1996 while the boilerplate says inception date, a minor internal mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete addition of one entity, though the form is mis-cited as '0098-052'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Additional Named Insureds endorsement (c085) and its 'no automatic coverage for newly acquired entities' proviso without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'effective on the inception date' language conflicts with the endorsement's own stated effective date of 01/01/1997.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'CMG - Brown Deer Campus' names a location rather than an identifiable legal person, which makes the scope of insured status uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a Named Insured directly rather than through Form 009-052 as the other additions do (c115, c120), and the endorsement's 01/01/1997 effective date conflicts with the inception-date boilerplate in c116.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement is dated 11/03/1997, after the policy period ended, yet is stated effective at inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It changes the named insured to 'Children's Health System, Inc.' (singular) — a one-letter change whose intended effect, correcting a name or substituting an entity, is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations, both copies, and every other endorsement name 'Children's Health Systems, Inc.', so which entity is the Item 1 insured depends on reconciling this late endorsement with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds two named campuses to Form 009-052; concrete, though 'campus' again denotes a place rather than an entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in mechanism with c085 and c115.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' is a compound and imprecise class description, and '$1,000,000/$3,000,000' is not tied to a stated per-claim/aggregate convention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This page is headed with the underlying policy number HPP-1996-4104-00 rather than the umbrella UML number, yet it changes the underlying limits that fix the Retained Limit (c034) and attachment point (c048), and it presupposes professional coverage that c082 excludes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reserved discretion to charge 'an appropriate premium' with no standard or cap; brief but open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same formula in the Contingent Excess endorsement (c103) and is not integrated with the Pay Plan Endorsement's fixed instalments.
